moved.sentence: **Heavy OS framework usage marks a boundary.** Files that import three or more OS-specific frameworks are tightly coupled to the platform runtime and likely belong in a platform-specific scope group.

judged.note: should-place-heavy-os-framework-users-in-platform-group keeps the three-or-more-frameworks threshold and 'typically' platform-group placement (the old 'likely'); the rationale keeps the tight-coupling-to-runtime reason.

moved.sentence: **Hardware APIs are natural boundaries.** Camera, GPS, Bluetooth, and biometric code has distinct permission requirements and testing needs — group these files together and mark the scope group as hardware-dependent.

judged.note: The two rules keep grouping camera/GPS/Bluetooth/biometric code and marking the group hardware-dependent; the rationale keeps the distinct permission and testing needs.

moved.sentence: **Network and persistence are separate concerns.** Files that talk to the network and files that write to local storage are often conflated — separate them unless they are part of a unified data synchronization layer.

judged.note: should-separate-network-and-persistence keeps the separation and its unified-sync-layer exception; the rationale keeps the often-conflated reason.

moved.sentence: **Third-party SDK boundaries.** If a third-party SDK is touched by more than 2–3 files, those files likely form a wrapper/adapter scope group that isolates the SDK from the rest of the codebase.

judged.note: should-identify-sdk-wrapper-groups keeps the more-than-2-3-files threshold and the likely wrapper/adapter group isolating the SDK.
should-identify-sdk-wrapper-groups keeps identifying the wrapper group explicitly (unkeyed, now SHOULD).

moved.sentence: **System dependencies that appear in many groups are cross-cutting.** Logging frameworks and analytics SDKs that appear across all candidate groups are not boundaries — they are cross-cutting concerns (see `cross-cutting-detection`).

judged.note: should-not-treat-widespread-dependencies-as-boundaries keeps that all-group logging and analytics SDKs are not boundaries but cross-cutting, with the cross-cutting-detection pointer.
